'''Natasha V. Raikhel'''<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/natasha-v-raikhel-tucxq1/ |title = Natasha Raikhel}}</ref> (born 1947) is a professor of plant cell biology at [[University of California, Riverside]] and a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].

==Early life and education==
Raikhel, the daughter of a [[surgeon]] and an [[Radiographer|X-Ray technician]], grew up in [[Leningrad]] in the [[Soviet Union]]. From a young age, she was cultivated to become a [[concert pianist]], until a teacher dissuaded her during her final year of high school from pursuing music as a career.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Cooper|first=Leigh|date=5 February 2018|title=Profile of Natasha V. Raikhel|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|volume=115|issue=8|pages=1672&ndash;1674|pmc=5828638|doi=10.1073/pnas.1721892115|pmid=29432184|bibcode=2018PNAS..115.1672C |doi-access=free}}</ref>  After transferring to a regular high school from the music conservatory, she studied various sciences day and night, finally earning high enough scores to attend [[Leningrad State University]] to study invertebrae biology.<ref name=":0" />  Raiklhel graduated in 1970 with her master's degree and went on to receive her Ph.D from the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in 1975.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Q&A"/><ref name="ASCB">{{Cite web|title=Natasha Raikhel|website=[[American Society for Cell Biology]]|date=August 3, 2009|url=http://ascb.org/files/profiles/natasha_Raikhel.pdf}}</ref><!-- There needs to be an addition of information here about the adversity that she encountered in getting her Ph.D. -->

== Immigrating to America ==
In 1978, she, her husband, and their son survived a deadly plane crash—which the airline refused to acknowledge had even taken place.<ref name=":0" />  The incident, alongside the death of her father and regular anti-Semitic encounters, convinced the couple to take their son abroad rather than to continue to live in the Soviet Union.<ref name=":0" />  Due to their [[Jew]]ish heritage, they obtained permission to emigrate shortly before the Soviet border closed for the last time concurrent with the [[Soviet invasion of Afghanistan]]. With the help of [[University of Georgia]] professor [[Jerome Paulin]], who had temporarily worked alongside Raikhel in Leningrad in the late 1970s, Raikhel and her family emigrated to [[Rome]] and then to [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] in 1979 as political refugees.<ref name="ASCB" /><ref name="NCBI">{{Cite journal|journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]]|date=December 28, 2010|volume=107|issue=52|pages=22381–22383|doi=10.1073/pnas.1018340108|title=Profile of Alexander S. Raikhel|first=Tinsley H.|last=Davis|pmc= 3012477|via=[[National Center for Biotechnology Information]]|pmid=21173217|bibcode=2010PNAS..10722381D|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Education career ==
Shortly after arriving Raikhel started her [[Postdoctoral researcher|post-doctoral work]] at University of Georgia, concluding in 1984 when she was hired by the University as an assistant research scientist in their [[botany]] department. Beginning in 1986, she taught at [[Michigan State University]]'s East Lansing campus as an assistant professor of botany. She was advanced to full professor in 1994.<ref name="CV" /> In 1996 Raikhel was awarded a [[Guggenheim fellowship]] for the study of plant sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Natasha V. Raikhel|url=http://www.gf.org/fellows/11927-natasha-v-raikhel|website=[[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]]|access-date=March 1, 2015}}</ref> She has done research related to [[SNAREs in plants|SNARE proteins in plants]], an understudied area, including Zheng et al 1999 in which she and her team found [[AtVTI1a]] to be essential to [[Golgi apparatus|Golgi]]⇄[[vacuole]] trafficking.<ref name="Raikhel-2017">{{cite journal | last=Raikhel | first=Natasha V. | author-link=Natasha Raikhel | title=Firmly Planted, Always Moving | journal=[[Annual Review of Plant Biology]] | publisher=[[Annual Reviews (publisher)|Annual Reviews]] | volume=68 | issue=1 | date=2017-04-28 | issn=1543-5008 | doi=10.1146/annurev-arplant-042916-040829 | pages=1–27| pmid=27860488 | doi-access=free }}</ref> In 2001, the Raikhel family moved to [[University of California, Riverside]] (UCR) where she teaches plant cell biology. In 2012 Raikhel was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] for "pioneering the use of novel genetic and biochemical techniques to elucidate the organization and function of the secretory system in plant cells."<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite press release|title=Plant Cell Biologist Receives Top Scientific Honor|first=Iqbal|last=Pittalwala|date=May 1, 2012|url=http://ucrtoday.ucr.edu/5777|publisher=University of California, Riverside}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=UCR professor elected to National Academy of Sciences|date=May 1, 2012|website=KESQ|url=http://www.kesq.com/news/UCR-professor-elected-to-National-Academy-of-Sciences/12389974}}</ref>  She holds the Ernst and Helen Leibacher Endowed Chair in Plant Molecular, Cell Biology & Genetics at UCR.<ref name="press">{{Cite news|title=Riverside: Plant cell biologist receives top scientific honor|date=May 26, 2012|newspaper=[[Press-Enterprise]]|url=https://www.pressenterprise.com/2012/05/26/riverside-plant-cell-biologist-receives-top-scientific-honor/}}</ref> She is the founding director of UCR's Center for Plant Cell Biology and the current director of UCR's Institute for Integrative Genome Biology.<ref>{{Cite press release|title=Researchers Receive High Honor From American Society of Plant Biologists|first=Iqbal|last=Pittalwala|date=April 26, 2013|url=http://ucrtoday.ucr.edu/14178}}</ref>

==Personal life==
She is an old and intimate friend of [[Susan R. Wessler]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://ucrtoday.ucr.edu/5777 |title = Plant Cell Biologist Receives Top Scientific Honor}}</ref> In 1989, she was diagnosed with [[breast cancer]] and received treatment for eight years before the cancer went into [[Remission (medicine)|remission]].<ref name="ASCB" />
